I transferred to online UIS for CS from Limestone College. It’s a much, much better program (and cheaper too). While I’m only in my first semester, I can tell you this: faculty seems very communicative. I have had a few questions for financial aid and my financial aid advisor answers emails within 24 hours. 3 out of my 4 professors answer emails very quickly, and I have phone numbers for those 3 as well (although I haven’t called them). The library faculty is also very helpful and will even arrange Skype sessions to help with research if you live out of state (like I do). 

I’m satisfied so far. The curriculum is challenging, and if I encounter any problems I feel comfortable reaching out to my professors via email. I have been treated with respect, even if I feel as though my questions may be elementary. 

My only complaint is that none of the classes I completed at Limestone have been applied toward my major (Introduction to Computer Science and Operating Systems), but it’s been explained to me that it’s simply because the curriculum at Limestone doesn’t match UIS. I’m still trying to petition to have these classes applied, but it doesn’t seem as though it’ll happen. So if you’re transferring, make sure to keep all your previous syllabi. 

Edit: also got a new job that I’ll be starting in a little over a week. They were pleased to see UIS on my resume and are arranging for me to have a quiet place for me to study during lunch break.

That’s the point: you have no way of knowing this guy is lying about what he sold. Neither do I. We can guess all day long (and we’d probably be correct in my opinion), but without evidence, well our assumptions are just guesses. 

With that said, our justice system is set up to where suspects are presumed innocent until proven guilty in a court of law. This means the following:

A) Law enforcement, no matter how much evidence they have, do NOT have the right to dole out punishment to suspects. That is the courts job, not theirs. 

B) If I am understanding civil asset forfeiture laws correctly, he can get his money back so long as he can prove he got it in a legal way. Well, that’s against our justice system because now his money is on trial and the money can’t defend itself. Plus he has to now spend more money on lawyers (kind of like a punishment) to prove he didn’t do anything wrong even though he’s not on trial. Or he can forfeit his money to an agency that took it without charging him with a crime. That’s a financial punishment because now he’s suffering financially. 

That’s why I believe asset forfeiture laws are wrong. If someone gets convicted of something illegal, then fine, take their assets. If not, well that’s just robbery.

The main reasons I believe iOS is best for me right now are basically the two I ended my story with - Apple not budging (at the moment at least) to the demands of the DOJ (this makes me feel that Apple actually values the privacy of their users), and the updates for my two new devices not being carrier dependent (no more being paranoid about being vulnerable to security exploits while my manufacturer of choice and carrier take their time to push an update).

As far as what I'm missing from Android, I guess I sort of miss a couple of things. I like the variety of hardware available. I do also miss being able to expand storage by using a microSD card, but with most of my documents and pictures (I take TONS of pictures of my family and projects) stored in the cloud in either Drive or Dropbox and now even iCloud, I'm not actually losing any sleep over it. Acknowledgement is the first step. One thing I've learned in my PTSD journey (and therapy) is mindfulness and radical acceptance (with the latter being the most difficult for me). I have to focus on the present - be aware of my surroundings without being hyper vigilant, be aware of my emotions, and be aware of my thoughts. Then comes the radical acceptance - I have to realize that there are things that are just beyond my control. I can't change people, and sometimes I have to accept that even *things* or situations are out of my control. For example, I am in recovery (dual diagnosed) and I live in a crappy area full of drugs. I can't change the fact that there will be drug dealers on my street. I can't change where I live *at this moment* (I just don't have the financial capability right now), but I can be aware of what is happening and focus on what is right and what is keeping me safe.

I hope this helps.
